senses.gloss:
Nai-ṣāda, a ‘man of Niṣāda,’ is mentioned in the Kauṣītaki
Brāhmaṇa (xxv. 15) and the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (xxx. 8).

Naiṣidha is the reading in the Śata atha Brāhmaṇa (ii. 3,
2, 1. 2) of the epithet of Naḍa, a king of the south. The later
form of the name is Naiṣadha; the St. Petersburg Dictionarv
suggests that its original form was Naiḥṣidha.
